title: Support Excel-style non-formula single-cell entries
description: Support worksheet cell-entry semantics in OxFml for inputs that do not begin with '='. Intended downstream behavior: formula entries still require leading '='; entries beginning with apostrophe are forced text with the apostrophe removed; otherwise parse exact numbers as Number, TRUE/FALSE as Logical, quoted string literals as Text using existing quote decoding, and default every other non-formula/non-known-type entry to Text. Examples: ABC, '=123, 12.1.1, x y z = 12.3 should be text; 123.4 should be number; TRUE should be logical. This should remove the need for DnaOneCalc host-side hand-evaluation of literal cell entries while preserving editor source fidelity.
design: Implemented WorksheetA1 cell-entry classification in the parser entry path, before normal formula parsing: leading '=' remains formula; leading apostrophe is forced text with the apostrophe removed; finite numeric entries become NumberLiteralExpr; TRUE/FALSE become logical IdentifierExpr; quoted string literals keep existing string decode behavior; all other non-formula entries become synthetic StringLiteralExpr text literals. Full-fidelity editor snapshots still project from the original lexer token stream, so source rendering remains exact while parse/bind/eval use the typed cell-entry interpretation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Spec text added to docs/spec/OXFML_DNA_ONECALC_DOWNSTREAM_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md Section 2.1A. 2. Editor test covers ABC, '=123, 12.1.1, x y z = 12.3, quoted string, number, TRUE, FALSE with no diagnostics and expected bound literal kind. 3. Runtime test verifies those entries publish Text/Number/Logical values through RuntimeEnvironment. 4. cargo test -p oxfml_core passes locally.

title: Rework parser trivia ownership and editor token fidelity
description:
A sequence of editor snapshot bugs shows a structural problem in OxFml parser/trivia ownership, not isolated missing skip/retain patches. Examples include leading trivia before the root equals token and significant whitespace/intersection cases such as '=A A'. The current parser consumes some whitespace as syntax-significant tokens, discards/reattaches other whitespace as trivia, and the editor snapshot is derived from the parse green tree rather than directly from a full-fidelity token stream. This creates repeated truncation and misclassification risks.

Required rework scope:
1. Audit the current lex -> parse -> attach_trivia_to_green_tree -> EditorSyntaxSnapshot pipeline and document ownership of every token class.
2. Define an invariant: editor syntax snapshots must preserve every non-EOF lexical token and every source character exactly once, either as token text or token trivia, including syntactically invalid tails.
3. Separate semantic parse consumption from full-fidelity editor token projection, or rework green-tree construction so full-fidelity tokens cannot be lost.
4. Treat whitespace intersection explicitly: '=A A' must keep the inter-reference whitespace as a syntax-significant intersection token while preserving editor rendering fidelity.
5. Add property/table-driven regression tests for leading trivia, trailing invalid tokens, whitespace intersection, ordinary intra-token trivia, array/call delimiters, unknown tokens, and partial-edit/incomplete formulas.
6. Avoid further one-off parser patches unless they are part of the declared rework.
7. Run cargo test -p oxfml_core and coordinate downstream DnaOneCalc after the rework lands.

Related handoff: ../DnaOneCalc/docs/handoffs/oxfml_leading_whitespace_truncation.md
Ownership note: This is OxFml parser/editor architecture work. DnaOneCalc must not mask missing source spans with host-side gap-fill.
design: Audit result: lexer is the only full source-fidelity owner. Parser/green tree are semantic syntax owners and may skip trivia, retain syntax-significant whitespace for intersection, or retain invalid tails for diagnostics. EditorSyntaxSnapshot must not derive character coverage from semantic green-tree children because parser ownership can intentionally omit or reclassify trivia. Rework decision: build EditorSyntaxSnapshot from GreenTreeRoot.full_fidelity_tokens, attach every lexer whitespace run as duplicated previous trailing / next leading trivia, and synthesize a zero-width Unknown token only for all-trivia sources so source text still tiles. Semantic parse and editor projection are now separated.
acceptance_criteria: 1. EditorSyntaxSnapshot documented source-tiling invariant. 2. Snapshot reconstruction test covers leading trivia, inter-reference whitespace, trailing invalid tokens, incomplete formulas, unknown/operator tails, string literals, error literals, and all-whitespace source. 3. '= a a' / '=A1 B1' / tab and multi-space intersection preserve source text through token+trivia projection. 4. cargo test -p oxfml_core passes. 5. Downstream DnaOneCalc ignored browser tests remain to be re-enabled after consuming this OxFml change.

title: Fix editor token snapshot truncation after leading whitespace
description:
DnaOneCalc reports that oxfml_core::consumer::editor::EditorEditService::apply_edit returns an EditorSyntaxSnapshot that drops tokens after the first non-trivia token when formula source begins with leading whitespace. Minimal input: 
=aaa. Expected tokens: '=' at span 1..2 with leading trivia '
', then identifier 'aaa' at span 2..5. Actual: only '=' is surfaced; 'aaa' is missing.

Scope:
1. Add focused oxfml_core regression tests for leading whitespace prefixes before formula tokens: newline, multiple newlines, space, tab, and a function call such as 
=SUM(1,2).
2. Inspect tokenizer, trivia attachment, and consumer editor snapshot-building paths for early-return/truncation after leading trivia.
3. Repair the OxFml-owned token/snapshot path; do not add DnaOneCalc host-side gap-fill.
4. Run focused editor tests and cargo test -p oxfml_core if feasible.
5. Record downstream coordination note so DnaOneCalc can remove ignored browser reproductions after consuming the fix.

Ownership note: This is an OxFml editor/token snapshot bug, not a DnaOneCalc rendering bug. The host renderer treats leading and non-leading snapshots identically; the missing identifier is absent upstream.
close_reason: Patched parser root leading-whitespace handling, added editor syntax snapshot regression coverage for newline/multiple-newline/space/tab/function-call prefixes, and validated with cargo test -p oxfml_core.

comments.author: GovertvanDrimmelen
comments.text: Similar-bug scan found another token-snapshot truncation risk: parser root diagnosed unexpected trailing tokens without retaining them in the green tree, so editor snapshots could drop invalid tails such as =1) or =SUM(1,2)). Added coverage and changed parse_formula_root to retain unexpected trailing tokens before EOF while still surfacing syntax diagnostics. Full cargo test -p oxfml_core passes.

title: W076 formula drill trace model for DnaOneCalc
description:
Parent epic for processing ../DnaOneCalc/docs/HANDOFF_OXFML_FORMULA_DRILL_TRACE_MODEL.md into OxFml-owned work.

DnaOneCalc's current formula drill-down has regressed into a mostly raw prepared-call display. The downstream audit command shows nested calls as top-level siblings, leaks preparation debug states such as eval=EagerValue for skipped branches, lacks source spans, lacks LET binding flow, lacks argument names, and cannot link errors or diagnostics to the causal expression.

OxFml owns formula structure, semantic evaluation, trace publication policy, source-span correlation, argument preparation, LET/LAMBDA binding, lazy branch disposition, operator/error causality, and public runtime facade shape. DnaOneCalc must not reconstruct those facts from formula text, private OxFml internals, or local function-registry mirrors.

This epic should create a drill-ready FormulaDrillTrace artifact or stable runtime projection that DnaOneCalc can consume directly for User and Developer views.

Inbound handoff: ../DnaOneCalc/docs/HANDOFF_OXFML_FORMULA_DRILL_TRACE_MODEL.md
Relevant local owner areas: consumer runtime facade, parser/source spans, semantic plan/evaluator trace, OxFunc registry argument metadata, replay-facing diagnostics.
design:
Epic design:
1. Keep the DnaOneCalc handoff as the parent external reference.
2. Split execution into two leaves: first the additive public contract, then the runtime emission/projection with focused evidence.
3. Treat the contract bead as spec_drafted until compile-checked packet types or runtime projection exist.
4. Treat DnaOneCalc host uptake as downstream integration work after OxFml emits the artifact; filing or updating a downstream handoff is not OxFml closure by itself.
5. Preserve lane ownership: OxFml owns formula structure/evaluation trace projection, OxFunc owns function metadata and function/operator semantics, DnaOneCalc owns UI mapping and host-facing verdict policy.
acceptance_criteria:
1. OxFml has an accepted narrow work plan for a public formula drill trace artifact with clear ownership boundaries.
2. The child bead for contract/model shape defines stable node ids, parent/child structure, source spans, argument roles/names, evaluation states, branch disposition, LET/LAMBDA binding records, error causality, diagnostics, and typed array/rich previews.
3. The child bead for runtime emission defines how RuntimeFormulaResult or an equivalent projection service exposes the trace without requiring DnaOneCalc to parse prepared_calls.
4. Minimal acceptance corpus is explicitly carried forward: =SUM(1,2,3), =SUM(IF(TRUE,2,3),4), =IF(FALSE,SUM(1,2),SUM(3,4)), =LET(x,1,y,2,SUM(x,y)), =1/0, =SEQUENCE(2,2), and =SUM(.
5. The plan preserves OxFml/OxFunc ownership: OxFml owns formula structure and evaluation trace projection; OxFunc metadata supplies argument names/roles where available; DnaOneCalc owns host UI mapping and final UX verdict after consuming the artifact.
6. Status reporting for this epic uses the three-axis doctrine and does not treat scaffolded schema text as implementation evidence.
notes: Created from DnaOneCalc formula drill trace handoff. This is an execution-planning epic only; it is not a completion claim.

title: W076 define FormulaDrillTrace V1 public contract
description:
Define the OxFml-owned public contract for a drill-ready formula evaluation trace requested by DnaOneCalc.

Problem to solve:
DnaOneCalc currently receives a flat prepared-call trace. That trace is valuable for evaluator debugging but is not a host-facing expression explanation tree. It cannot reliably show nested expression structure, branch choice, LET binding flow, source-code focus, argument names, skipped expressions, coercion/preparation detail, partial-call diagnostics, or error causality.

Scope:
1. Decide whether the public surface is a new RuntimeFormulaResult.formula_drill_trace field or a stable projection service over RuntimeFormulaResult and adjacent runtime artifacts.
2. Specify FormulaDrillTrace schema_id, formula_stable_id, source_text, root_node_id, nodes, evaluation_order, diagnostics, final_value, and optional capability/version fields.
3. Specify FormulaDrillTraceNode fields for deterministic node id, parent id, child ids, source span, expression text, kind, function/operator identity, argument ordinal/name/role, user/developer labels, evaluation state, before/after coercion values, returned/published values, typed error, and prepared-call/prepared-argument correlation.
4. Define node kinds for formula root, function call, operator call, argument, literal, name reference, LET binding, LAMBDA binding, array literal, spill/rich-value summary, error, and diagnostic placeholder.
5. Define evaluation/disposition vocabulary for evaluated, bound, skipped, short-circuited, omitted, pending, blocked, error, taken branch, skipped branch, not reached, error while choosing, and error while evaluating branch.
6. Define how OxFunc registry metadata supplies argument names/roles and how OxFml records explicit fallback-to-ordinal when metadata is unavailable.
7. Define typed preview rules for arrays and rich values: shape, compact preview, truncation flag, and capability/result-class facts. The host must not parse display strings to recover shape.
8. Define diagnostics linkage for partial or invalid formulas so incomplete calls can still produce source-linked placeholder nodes.
9. State non-goals: no DnaOneCalc parse-tree reconstruction, no host-local IF/LET inference, no private binder internals in the public API, no closure claim without replay/test evidence.

Likely docs/code touched:
- docs/spec/OXFML_CONSUMER_INTERFACE_AND_FACADE_CONTRACT_V1.md
- docs/spec/OXFML_PUBLIC_API_AND_RUNTIME_SERVICE_SKETCH.md
- docs/spec/OXFML_DNA_ONECALC_DOWNSTREAM_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md
- crates/oxfml_core/src/consumer/runtime/mod.rs if compile-checked public packets are introduced in this bead.
design:
Use an additive V1 artifact rather than changing prepared_calls semantics. PreparedCall remains an evaluator/preparation trace; FormulaDrillTrace becomes the host-facing expression explanation artifact.

Preferred model:
- FormulaDrillTrace is tree-first, with a separate evaluation_order list.
- Node ids are deterministic within one parse/evaluation result and should be stable for equivalent source/runtime context where practical, but the first contract should not over-claim cross-version identity.
- Source spans use byte offsets into source_text unless the existing editor/runtime span type already specifies a stronger unit. The chosen unit must be documented and used consistently.
- Function/operator semantic names come from resolved call sites and OxFunc registry metadata, not from DnaOneCalc mirrors.
- Branch and LET/LAMBDA flow are OxFml-owned semantic projection, not UI decoration.
- Developer fields may expose preparation/coercion and prepared_call correlation; User labels should be semantic and not leak raw eval-mode debug text.

Contract should include a projection-loss field or capture-loss note if a node cannot be fully linked to source or prepared-call evidence in the first slice. Such loss must be explicit and test-visible.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Spec text defines FormulaDrillTrace V1 with tree structure, node ids, source spans, node kinds, evaluation states, branch dispositions, argument names/roles, LET/LAMBDA binding nodes, diagnostics links, error causality, coercion fields, and typed array/rich previews.
2. The spec explicitly classifies prepared_calls as lower-level evaluator/preparation trace, not a sufficient DnaOneCalc drill tree.
3. The spec states that DnaOneCalc must consume FormulaDrillTrace or its projection and must not reconstruct parse/evaluation semantics locally.
4. The spec includes the seven-case minimal acceptance corpus and expected structural facts for each case.
5. If compile-checked Rust packet types are added, they are additive under consumer::runtime and do not expose private parser/binder/evaluator internals.
6. Reviewed inbound observations line is recorded in the workset/status note: OxFunc notes reviewed; OxCalc notes reviewed; DnaOneCalc handoff processed.
7. No implementation/closure language is used for spec-only work; status remains in_progress or spec_drafted until runtime emission and deterministic evidence exist.

title: W076 emit FormulaDrillTrace from runtime facade with corpus evidence
description:
Implement the first OxFml runtime projection that emits FormulaDrillTrace for the DnaOneCalc drill-down corpus.

Problem to solve:
The current RuntimeFormulaResult.evaluation.trace.prepared_calls list is flat and evaluation-order-oriented. DnaOneCalc needs an OxFml-owned structural trace where nested calls are nested, skipped branches are explicit, LET bindings are shown as bindings, source spans link rows to formula text, and errors identify the smallest causal expression.

Scope:
1. Add the public field or projection service selected by the contract bead to the consumer runtime facade.
2. Build the structural trace from OxFml-owned formula artifacts and evaluator hooks, not by reparsing source text inside DnaOneCalc.
3. Preserve parent/child structure for nested calls and operator expressions.
4. Emit branch disposition for IF-like lazy forms, at minimum enough to distinguish taken, skipped/not evaluated, and error states for the acceptance corpus.
5. Emit LET binding records for name/value pairs and body expressions, with name references resolving visibly to bound values where the evaluator already has that truth.
6. Emit operator nodes and causal errors for division by zero and equivalent first-slice operator failures.
7. Attach source spans to calls, arguments, literals, operators, LET bindings, diagnostics, and partial placeholders wherever the existing parser/editor span substrate can support it; record explicit capture loss otherwise.
8. Use OxFunc registry/call metadata for argument names such as logical_test, value_if_true, value_if_false, number1, number2, and flag ordinal fallback if needed.
9. Emit typed array/rich previews for at least SEQUENCE(2,2), including shape and truncation/preview fields rather than display-string parsing.
10. Keep prepared_call/prepared_argument correlation fields for developer view and replay debugging, but do not make DnaOneCalc depend on raw prepared_calls for structure.
11. Add focused tests or fixture snapshots for the minimal acceptance corpus.

Likely files touched:
- crates/oxfml_core/src/consumer/runtime/mod.rs
- crates/oxfml_core/src/eval/mod.rs and adjacent trace/projection helpers
- parser/red-tree/span helpers if source-span plumbing gaps are found
- crates/oxfml_core/tests/*w076* or equivalent focused runtime tests
- docs/worksets/W076_formula_drill_trace_model.md or a status note if a workset doc is created.
design:
Build this as an additive projection over the current runtime path.

Implementation strategy:
1. Start with a trace builder that receives the source text, existing parse/bind/semantic artifacts, and evaluation events.
2. For function/operator evaluation, allocate a drill node at expression entry and close it with returned/published value or error on exit.
3. For lazy forms, create child argument/branch nodes even when a branch is skipped; skipped branches should carry expression text/span and evaluation_state=Skipped instead of debug preparation text.
4. For LET, create a LET call/frame node, binding child nodes for each name/value pair, and a body child node. References to bound names should carry a source span and resolved value when available.
5. For errors, link FormulaDrillError.causal_node_id to the smallest node where the evaluator can prove cause; for =1/0 this should be the divide operator node with the right operand visible as zero.
6. For incomplete formulas, allow parser/binder diagnostics to create DiagnosticPlaceholder or partial FunctionCall nodes so the UI can focus a meaningful source span.
7. Treat capture-loss honestly. If first-slice source spans or causal links cannot be produced for a family, expose a typed missing/capture-loss field and keep that family outside closure claims.

Do not introduce function-specific semantic fast paths in OxFml. Operator/function outcomes still come from existing OxFml/OxFunc evaluation; this bead only projects already-owned semantic facts into a host-facing artifact.
acceptance_criteria:
1. RuntimeFormulaResult or an approved public projection service exposes FormulaDrillTrace for successful and diagnostic-producing formula evaluations.
2. =SUM(1,2,3) emits one SUM function node under the formula root, named number arguments, and final value 6.
3. =SUM(IF(TRUE,2,3),4) emits SUM as the root call, IF nested under SUM argument 1, value_if_false marked skipped, and evaluation_order separate from tree order.
4. =IF(FALSE,SUM(1,2),SUM(3,4)) emits the true branch as skipped and the false branch as evaluated with nested SUM result 7.
5. =LET(x,1,y,2,SUM(x,y)) emits LET binding nodes for x and y, a body node, nested SUM, and name references resolving visibly to 1 and 2.
6. =1/0 emits a divide/operator node, left/right operand nodes, final #DIV/0!, and an error record whose causal_node_id points to the divide node or a more specific zero-denominator node if modeled.
7. =SEQUENCE(2,2) emits typed array shape and preview data without requiring display-string parsing.
8. =SUM( emits a partial call or diagnostic placeholder with source-span-linked diagnostics for missing/invalid argument and expected delimiter behavior.
9. Tests assert parent/child relationships, source spans for representative nodes, argument labels, branch dispositions, LET binding flow, causal error link, and typed array preview.
10. Validation includes focused W076 tests and cargo test -p oxfml_core before any gate/closure claim.
11. DnaOneCalc follow-up handoff or status note is prepared after the OxFml artifact exists, explicitly saying host uptake remains a downstream lane and does not close until DnaOneCalc acknowledges consumption.
